text:
ALLEN JOSEPH BROUSSARD
Published 12:00 pm Thursday, November 5, 2026
|

|
Allen Joseph Broussard, 90, passed away peacefully on October 28, 2026.
Born on May 23, 1936, in New Iberia, Louisiana, to Wade Joseph Broussard Sr. and Anna Mae (Savoy) Broussard. He developed a love of music at an early age, teaching himself to play guitar at seven years old, a passion that remained with him throughout his life.
On May 1, 1960, he married Bonnie Elaine Arnaud in New Iberia, Louisiana. Their marriage of more than 66 years was centered on faith, friendship, family, and serving others.
In June 1960, Allen entered the United States Army and served honorably until June 1962. During his service, he received the Army Commendation Medal for improved accounting practices.
After his military service, Allen built a career in accounting. He began with Arthur Andersen, later served as an accounting professor at Saint Joseph’s College, and practiced as a Certified Public Accountant.
Allen’s Christian faith remained central throughout his life. He was a founding member of the Saturday Men’s Bible Study in the 1980s and also participated in the Thursday Morning Men’s Bible Study. These groups provided lasting friendships and opportunities for fellowship and service.
Music remained one of Allen’s greatest joys. He played guitar, piano, saxophone, and clarinet and enjoyed singing. Alongside Bonnie, he shared music at weddings, nursing homes, Jasper County Alternacare, and care centers. He also cherished many years of friendship and music with John Baumann, including their regular Wednesday gatherings.
Allen was known for his generosity, sense of humor, and ability to make people feel welcome. Above all, he loved his family. Known by many titles throughout his life, his favorite was “Paw Paw.”
He was preceded in death by his parents; sisters, Doris Vann, Sally Harper, and Virginia Broussard; and brother, Wade Broussard Jr.
He is survived by his wife, Bonnie Elaine Broussard; daughters, Robin Lynne (Alan) Brunton, Carrie Ann (Mike) Dorton, Sheila Renee Broussard (fiancé Mark Diguilio), and Marsha Campbell, who joined their home as a foster child at age seven and remained family thereafter; grandchildren Ryan (Megan) Dorton, Sarah (Aaron) Hooten, Adam (Jenna) Brunton, Rachal Dorton, Bryce Dorton, Trey Dorton, and Xander DiGuilio; eight great-grandchildren; and siblings Gloria Broussard, Warren Broussard, and Willien Broussard.
Allen will be remembered for his faith, kindness, music, laughter, and devotion to family and friends.
Visitation will be Monday, Nov. 2, 2026 from 10 a.m. until noon at Steinke Funeral Home of Rensselaer. Funeral services will follow at noon at the funeral home with Rev. Kenin Smith officiating. Burial with military honors will follow at Weston Cemetery.
In lieu of flowers, memorials may be made to Franciscan Hospice Care.
For full obituary, please visit https://www.steinkefuneralhome.com/obituaries/allen-broussard.
